Every email the system sends
Every email the system sends, in the order a lead meets them.
How to use it: Change any words you like. Keep the words in {curly brackets}: they are filled in for each lead. When you are done, tell Claude 'done'. Nothing goes live until you say so.
When you say 'done', everything in this doc counts as approved, except the first replies marked 'Not approved yet'. Emails still only go out after you tell Claude 'go live'.
Approved does not mean every email goes out on its own. Only these do, once you say 'done' and 'go live': the main text of the five AI agents first replies (a yes, 'tell me more', 'send me info', a booking link ask and a price question); the main text of follow-up emails 1 to 10, with the lines picked for the lead's offer; and the main text of the Locked in booking confirmation, only after the call is booked in GoHighLevel at exactly the time they picked. Everything else comes to you as a draft: every other version of any email, every reply offering other times, the replies about a time that is already taken or a call that is already booked, the Locked in version for another time zone, the show-rate reminders and no-show emails (paused since October 5), any nurture email, and the older offers' first replies. Every send check still applies.
If a sentence appears in many emails (like the time-offer line in first replies), changing it once is enough; it changes everywhere. If you change two copies differently, Claude will ask.
Leave the small grey tags at the end of each heading as they are: they tell Claude which email is which. Grey lines marked note or section are only there to help you read.
Type your changes straight into the text: no suggesting mode, no strikethrough, no highlights or text colours. Claude reads only the words, so a doc with any of those is not approved; Claude asks you instead.
Other versions of an email, like 'If there are no free times:', show what they change: a grey line quotes the lines of the email above that they replace or leave out, and the lines under it are the new ones. The versions with example dates and times are written out in full.
Words in brackets: {first_name} their first name, {company} their company, {slots} two open times, {slot} one time, {zoom_link} the call link, {original_subject} the subject of their email. The cold emails use Instantly's double brackets, like {{firstName}}.
If we don't have their first name, 'Hey {first_name},' becomes 'Hey there,'. If we don't have their company name, {company} becomes 'your business'. A follow-up email that names the company is held until we have it. In a referral reply with no name, {referral_name} becomes 'the right person' and {referral_first_name} becomes 'them'.
How times are written
Every time is Central (CT). The engine writes them like this:
{slots}: Tue 12:05pm or Thu 4:30pm CT (just Tue 12:05pm CT when only one time is free)
{slot}: Tue 12:05pm (the email adds CT after it)
{slot1} and {slot2}: Tue 12:05pm CT
{when_ct}: Tue, Jan 8 at 12:05pm CT, and in another timezone Tue, Jan 8 at 12:05pm CT (1:05pm ET)
{time_ct}: 12:05pm CT
{asked_time}: the time they asked for, in their own zone, like Mon 10:45am ET
{lead_local_time}: their own time, like 1:05pm ET (only added when they are not on Central)
{alt_slots}: like {slots}; when the times are in another week the dates are added, like Tue Jan 15 12:05pm or Thu Jan 17 4:30pm CT
Zones are written CT, ET, MT, PT, and MST for Arizona.
Exactly how the engine writes times, from its own code (part of every email with a time in it): (tag: formats.1)
Example times: Mon Jan 7 9:45, Tue Jan 8 12:05 and Thu Jan 10 16:30, 2030, Central (America/Chicago). This block is the same on every template that has a time or slot in it.
Two times, {slots} and {alt_slots}: Tue 12:05pm or Thu 4:30pm CT
One time, {slots}, {alt_slots}, {slot1} and {slot2}: Tue 12:05pm CT
A time without its zone, {slot}: Tue 12:05pm | Thu 4:30pm | Mon 9:45am
A counter-proposal that crosses a week, {alt_slots}: Tue Jan 15 12:05pm or Thu Jan 17 4:30pm CT
The time the lead proposed, in the zone they wrote it in, {asked_time}: America/Chicago = Mon 9:45am CT | America/New_York = Mon 10:45am ET | America/Denver = Mon 8:45am MT | America/Los_Angeles = Mon 7:45am PT
The time the lead proposed, when the counter-proposal crosses a week, {asked_time}: America/Chicago = Mon Jan 7 9:45am CT | America/New_York = Mon Jan 7 10:45am ET | America/Denver = Mon Jan 7 8:45am MT | America/Los_Angeles = Mon Jan 7 7:45am PT
The lead's own time after the call time, {lead_local_time}: America/Chicago = (nothing added) | America/New_York = (1:05pm ET your time) | America/Denver = (11:05am MT your time) | America/Los_Angeles = (10:05am PT your time) | America/Phoenix = (11:05am MST your time)
The call time, {when_ct}: Tue, Jan 8 at 12:05pm CT
The call time when the lead's timezone is known, {when_ct}: America/Chicago = Tue, Jan 8 at 12:05pm CT | America/New_York = Tue, Jan 8 at 12:05pm CT (1:05pm ET) | America/Denver = Tue, Jan 8 at 12:05pm CT (11:05am MT) | America/Los_Angeles = Tue, Jan 8 at 12:05pm CT (10:05am PT) | America/Phoenix = Tue, Jan 8 at 12:05pm CT (11:05am MST)
The clock time only, {time_ct}: 12:05pm CT | 4:30pm CT
Zone labels: America/Chicago = CT | America/New_York = ET | America/Denver = MT | America/Los_Angeles = PT | America/Phoenix = MST
Doc build: e95a04557f8a8faa (tag: X-BUILD)
Cold emails in Instantly (live copy, checked 2026-09-23) (section)
Instantly sends these. Step 2 goes out 3 days after step 1, in the same email thread, and only if they haven't replied. {{personalization}} is the opening line written for each lead. (note)
Cleaning, reactivation offer (section)
Campaign: 2026 Cleaning - Client Reactivation. Sends between 7am and 7pm Eastern time. (note)
Step 1: first email (tag: instantly.cleaning_reactivation.step1)
Subject: {{firstName}}, question (tag: instantly.cleaning_reactivation.step1/subject)
{{personalization}}

Know this is out of left field, if I could help recover the money from accounts that cancelled or stopped renewing their contracts in exchange for a commission on the accounts I bring back, would you be open? I work mostly on performance and am building my network.

About me: I build client reactivation systems. I built a similar system for a commercial roofer doing $150M/year. I recovered about $6M worth of contracts within 6 months. Would cost you nothing upfront.

Let me know.

Thanks,
Lorenzo
Step 2: 3 days later, if they haven't replied (tag: instantly.cleaning_reactivation.step2)
Subject: (tag: instantly.cleaning_reactivation.step2/subject)
No subject of its own: it goes as a reply in the same thread. (note)
Hey {{firstName}},

Checking in, in case the first one got buried. Quick version:
- I want to build a reactivation system for {{companyName}}. Goal is to bring back the accounts that cancelled or stopped renewing, without you chasing anyone.
- I did this for a commercial roofer doing $150M/yr and recovered about $6M in contracts in 6 months.
- Nothing up front. I only take a commission on the accounts I bring back.

Worth a quick 15 minute call? Just reply yes and I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks for the time,
Lorenzo

First reply when a lead replies interested (section)
The system picks one of these when a lead answers a cold email and sounds interested or asks a question, by their offer and what they asked. (note)
For the AI agents offer, once you say 'done' and then 'go live', the main text of the replies to a yes, 'tell me more', 'send me info', a booking link ask and a price question goes out on its own. Their three versions (no free times, a time they asked for that works, a time they asked for that doesn't) come to you as drafts, and so do a referral reply and any other question. The first replies for the older six offers are not approved yet: they stay drafts you write yourself until they are rewritten. (note)

Follow-up emails (section)
For a lead who went quiet after your first reply, in the order below. The first goes out the business day after your first reply; each one goes out at 10am Central on a business day, and they stop as soon as the lead books, replies or asks to stop. The main text of each, with the line picked for the lead's offer, goes out on its own after 'go live'; any other version comes to you as a draft. (note)
Follow-up email 1 (tag: cadence.e1)
Subject: Re: {original_subject} (tag: cadence.e1/subject)
If their email had no subject: Re: {first_name}, question. If we also don't have their first name: Re: your reply. (note)
Hey {first_name},

The time slots I sent got filled. Here are 2 more, let me know if they work: {slots}.

Lorenzo
Follow-up email 2 (tag: cadence.e2)
{research_line} is one of the lines right below this email, picked by the lead's offer. (note)
Read only: {research_line} can also be a line written for each lead by AI (cadence.e2.research_line). It has no fixed words to show here, so saying 'done' does not approve it, and an email carrying one is held, never sent. (note)
Subject: Re: {original_subject} (tag: cadence.e2/subject)
If their email had no subject: Re: {first_name}, question. If we also don't have their first name: Re: your reply. (note)
Hey {first_name},

{research_line}

Fifteen minutes is enough for me to show you how this would run for {company}. Let me know when a good time is to get a call on the books.

Lorenzo
Research fallback: reactivation offers (line used inside Follow-up email 2) (tag: cadence.e2.research_fallback.reactivation)
The quickest place to start is usually the accounts that already know you and went quiet.
Research fallback: outbound offers (line used inside Follow-up email 2) (tag: cadence.e2.research_fallback.outbound)
The quickest place to start is usually the prospects who are in market right now.
Research fallback: AI agents offer (line used inside Follow-up email 2) (tag: cadence.e2.research_fallback.ai_agents)
The quickest place to start is usually wherever the most money is slipping through right now.

Observation: cleaning (reactivation) (line used inside Follow-up email 9) (tag: cadence.e9.observation.cleaning_reactivation)
An account that cancelled or never signed already knows your name, so it's usually an easier conversation than a brand-new lead.
Observation: cleaning (outbound) (line used inside Follow-up email 9) (tag: cadence.e9.observation.cleaning_outbound)
A company moving into new space has to sort out cleaning around move-in.
Observation: bookkeeping (reactivation) (line used inside Follow-up email 9) (tag: cadence.e9.observation.bookkeeping_reactivation)
Quarterly estimates, year-end and tax season each give you a natural reason to check back in with former clients and old inquiries.
Observation: bookkeeping (outbound) (line used inside Follow-up email 9) (tag: cadence.e9.observation.bookkeeping_outbound)
A company posting a part-time bookkeeper job has already said out loud it needs help with its books.
Observation: recruiting (reactivation) (line used inside Follow-up email 9) (tag: cadence.e9.observation.recruiting_reactivation)
Clients who hired through you before, or almost did, already know how you work, so they're an easier conversation than any cold account.
Observation: recruiting (outbound) (line used inside Follow-up email 9) (tag: cadence.e9.observation.recruiting_outbound)
An open specialty role on a job board is a hiring manager saying in public they need someone.
Observation: AI agents offer (line used inside Follow-up email 9) (tag: cadence.e9.observation.ai_agents)
Quotes and proposals that went out and never got an answer are usually the first thing I'd hand to an agent.

Booking emails (section)
These answer a lead who writes back about a time for the call. Only the main text of the Locked in booking confirmation goes out on its own, and only after the call is booked in GoHighLevel at exactly the time they picked. Everything else here comes to you as a draft: its version for another time zone, every reply offering other times, and the replies about a time that is already taken or a call that is already booked. (note)
Booking confirmation, with Zoom link (tag: booking.confirmation.zoom_link)
When they pick a time that works, once the call is booked in GoHighLevel at exactly that time. Used when the call has a Zoom link. (note)
Subject: Re: {original_subject} (tag: booking.confirmation.zoom_link/subject)
If their email had no subject: Re: {first_name}, question. If we also don't have their first name: Re: your reply. (note)
Hey {first_name},

Locked in {slot} CT, invite on the way. Here is the Zoom link:
{zoom_link}

I will keep it to 15 minutes.

Lorenzo

Instead of "Locked in {slot} CT, invite on the way. Here is the Zoom link:": (note)
Locked in {slot} CT ({lead_local_time} your time), invite on the way. Here is the Zoom link:

Upwork pricing lines (section)
Your Upwork follow-up drafts can only quote a price that is written here. Right now there is none, so drafts never state a price. Write one price per box, the way you would say it to a client. Leave a box empty if you don't need it. (note)
Pricing line 1 (tag: U-PRICE-1)

Pricing line 2 (tag: U-PRICE-2)

Pricing line 3 (tag: U-PRICE-3)

After you finish (tag: X-AFTER)
1. Tell Claude "done". Claude reads this doc, puts your wording into the system and tests it. It then shows you any line a send check would stop, for example an exclamation mark or a price that is not on your offer sheet.
2. Nothing goes live until you tell Claude "go live".
3. Only you can do these, whenever you have a minute: change the passwords and keys that were saved in the code, and register your texting number (A2P).
4. Say "yes" to Claude for any of these and Claude does them: create the Upwork pipeline in GoHighLevel, start the 8:30 Upwork morning drafts, and send test alerts to your phone during the test week.
